A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Entropy and retain the same central entropy-matching framework. The text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison, including identification of material moved or combined in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model experiments on Gaussian and warped Gaussian mixtures in Section 7, plus a numerical dice simulation in Appendix A.1.

after.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture, MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments in Section 6 and Appendices D–E, including training curves, entropy measurements and generated images.

M1.justification: The entropy-matching reverse drift, denoising objective and neural-entropy estimator are retained. v2 adds the noise-scaled VPx forward-process variant (Eq. 24) and a class-conditioned image-model instantiation. These are limited adaptations of the existing framework; the newly documented density-estimation calculation does not establish a replacement of v1's previously mentioned procedure.

E1.justification: v1 concentrates on low-dimensional Gaussian and warped Gaussian mixtures. v2 retains Gaussian mixtures and adds unconditional MNIST generation and class-conditioned CIFAR-10 generation, substantially extending evaluation to structured image data. The warped-mixture experiments and illustrative dice simulation are absent from v2.

E2.justification: The entropy-matching versus score-matching comparison remains: v1 Figures 6–7 are combined in v2 Figure 9. v2 additionally evaluates the Straight Line diffusion process alongside VP and VPx in Gaussian-mixture comparisons, and compares VP with Straight Line on MNIST. This is a limited expansion of the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds Gaussian evaluations in dimensions 3, 6 and 9 alongside the retained 4–8-dimensional comparison. New protocols sweep training-set sizes, train MNIST models for 600 epochs and CIFAR-10 models for 200 epochs, and use cross-entropy for MNIST. Figure 18 controls image comparisons with the same ten initial noise vectors across sample-count settings. These are additional protocols, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds extensive analyses of training-time entropy absorption, forward-process entropy load, sample-count scaling and sparse-data overfitting. Figures 12–17 examine image entropy-production profiles and contrast image-model scaling with Gaussian-mixture MLP behavior. The controlled CIFAR-10 samples provide an additional case study. Conversely, v1's warped-mixture sensitivity analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v1 does not report repeated-training seeds or uncertainty bands. v2 Appendix E reports four seeds varying weight initialization and training-data order, averages the measurements, and identifies shaded bands as one standard deviation. This practice covers all models except those in the retained Figure 9 comparison; it does not establish additional runs for that comparison.

E6.justification: Although the original Gaussian entropy-versus-KL curves remain in v2 Figure 9, substantial new results appear. Figure 10 reports roughly two orders of magnitude more entropy for VPx/SL than VP, with slower learning and poorer reconstruction. Figures 1 and 16 report approximately logarithmic entropy growth with image sample counts, absent in the Gaussian/MLP experiment. Warped-mixture results and the dice simulation are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds discrete random-walk reversal and entropy derivations, explicit growth/Lipschitz/Novikov assumptions, and free-energy and density-bound calculations. The maximum-entropy dice derivation is removed, while much of the original KL-bound and H-theorem material is relocated. Additionally, v1's Vaikuntanathan–Jarzynski inequality, Eq. (3.2), becomes an equality in v2 Eq. (71), without stated additional conditions.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds entropy matching as a new diffusion scheme and a test bench for network encoding capacity. v2 makes efficient compression of image ensembles a central claim, supported by the newly asserted approximately logarithmic growth of neural entropy with training-set size. This substantially expands the contribution beyond the retained thermodynamic interpretation.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive interpretations involving image-manifold dimensionality, inductive biases and sparse-data overfitting to explain differences between image models and Gaussian-mixture MLPs. It explicitly acknowledges that logarithmic scaling lacks an explanation and that entropy measurements near zero diffusion time require care. Appendix E.2 also clarifies that reported density calculations substitute a lower bound for true log densities and are noisy for images.

D1.justification: v1 defers its likelihood-estimation method and code release. v2 supplies the density-bound derivation and Monte Carlo procedure, MLP widths, hardware and training-time information, diffusion-time cutoffs, sampling instructions and a code-availability link. These substantially improve documentation without proving that the earlier procedure changed. However, v2 does not repeat v1's explicit VP beta endpoints.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly relates entropy matching to Flow Matching and substantially expands positioning around generalization, Schrödinger bridges, associative memory, language-model compression and scaling laws. Earlier discussion and citations concerning renormalization and early-universe examples disappear. These changes extend beyond bibliography formatting or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around information storage and image ensembles. The main narrative now proceeds through Schrödinger's thought experiment and separates transport from storage experiments. Much of the former main-text theory moves into Appendices B–D, experimental documentation becomes Appendix E, and the contents moves after the references.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the visual presentation with compact inline summary plots, multiple training-curve panels and CIFAR-10 image grids. v1 Figures 6–7 are merged into v2 Figure 9; several explanatory figures move to appendices. The diffusion-cycle, warped-mixture and dice displays are removed. The document also adopts a more compact conference-style layout.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves image-model experiments as future work and defers essential likelihood-estimation details. v2 supplies image experiments, four-seed uncertainty reporting and an inspectable density-bound calculation with implementation and code-access information, substantially strengthening empirical support and reproducibility. Removing the warped-mixture diagnostic and the unexplained strengthening of Eq. (71) are drawbacks, and logarithmic scaling remains unexplained, but the overall evidential and documentation gains outweigh them.
